newsitem.title: JAPAN: E.Asia Grain - Traders awaiting USDA report.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grain - Traders awaiting USDA report.

text.p: A firming freight rate is expected to encourage purchases by East Asian grain importers, but they are generally expected to hold back until the U.S. Department of Agriculture's crop report on Wednesday, regional traders said on Monday.

Japanese traders have so far covered nearly 60 percent of their requirements for U.S. corn for the April-June shipment. Premiums for U.S. corn were quoted at about 95 U.S. cents a bushel over the CBOT May contract.
U.S. Gulf/Japan freight rates firmed last week to $24.65 per tonne for nearby shipment and $25 after April, a result of stable vessel demand from the steel and coal industry, traders said.
A trader with a foreign grain trading house in Seoul said the freight rate from the Pacific Northwest rose to $14 a tonne from $12-$12.50 a week ago because of stable vessel demand.
"We basically expect corn's fundamentals to soften in the near term. But the firming freight rate will encourage buyers to cover," a corn trader at a major trade house said.

China's central grain agency is offering corn to Japan at $135 per tonne on FOB basis at Dalian port, but this is not competitive with U.S. supplies, traders said. No deals for Chinese corn by Japanese traders were confirmed.

"Some regional grain exporters in China are hinting to us about cheaper export prices (than those of the central grain buying agency). But the Beijing authority is pressuring them not to discount," another corn trader said.

Some South Korean corn buyers' groups are likely to purchase up to 112,000 tonnes of corn this week for shipment in April, but others are expected to hold back until the release of a USDA report, traders said.
The USDA's 1996/97 supply/demand report is due out on Wednesday.
"We have one 50,000 tonne cargo left to be covered for shipment in April," said a trader with South Korea's National Livestock Cooperative Federation (NLCF).
He said the federation was aiming to buy the corn from Argentina since its planned shipment would coincide with the main Argentine export season.
Another trader said several feed milling companies have to jointly buy one 50,000 tonne cargo of Argentine corn and one 12,000 tonne cargo of Chinese corn for shipment in April.
Japanese importers are buying U.S. soybean for April shipment. Premiums for U.S. soybeans were quoted at about 115 U.S. cents a bushel over the CBOT March, trader said.
